title: Understanding and overcoming phobias, with Martin Antony, PhD

sentences.en: Are you afraid of heights?
sentences.zh: 你恐高吗？

sentences.en: Do you hyperventilate at the thought of a flu shot?
sentences.zh: 一想到要打流感疫苗，你就会呼吸急促吗？

sentences.en: Do you go out of your way to avoid elevators and other small, enclosed spaces?
sentences.zh: 你会特意避开电梯和其他狭小密闭的空间吗？

sentences.en: Have you driven across the country because you're too frightened to fly?
sentences.zh: 你曾因为害怕坐飞机而选择开车横跨整个国家吗？

sentences.en: Or avoided a particular driving route because you're terrified of bridges?
sentences.zh: 或者因为极度害怕桥梁而绕开某条特定的行车路线？

sentences.en: All of these are examples of what psychologists call specific phobias, which constitute one of the most common forms of anxiety disorder.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是心理学家所说的特定恐惧症的例子，它们是焦虑症最常见的形式之一。

sentences.en: Studies have found that anywhere from 9% to 13% of people experience a specific phobia at some point in their lives.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，9% 到 13% 的人在其一生中的某个阶段都会经历某种特定恐惧症。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, although effective treatments are available, far fewer people receive treatment than could benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，尽管有有效的治疗方法，但接受治疗的人数远远少于能够从中受益的人数。

sentences.en: So what are phobias and how do they differ from fears?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是恐惧症？它们与恐惧有何不同？

sentences.en: What are some of the most common phobias and how common are they?
sentences.zh: 最常见的恐惧症有哪些？它们的患病率有多高？

sentences.en: Where do phobias come from?
sentences.zh: 恐惧症从何而来？

sentences.en: Are you born with them or are they learned?
sentences.zh: 它们是天生带来的还是后天学来的？

sentences.en: What treatments are available for phobias and how well do they work?
sentences.zh: 有哪些针对恐惧症的治疗方法？它们的疗效如何？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Martin Antony, a professor in the Department of Psychology at Toronto Metropolitan
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是多伦多都会大学心理学系教授马丁·安东尼博士。

sentences.en: University.
sentences.zh: 大学。

sentences.en: He also holds part-time or adjunct faculty appointments at McMaster University and the University of Toronto.
sentences.zh: 他还曾在麦克马斯特大学和多伦多大学担任兼职或客座教职。

sentences.en: And he was the founding director of the Anxiety Treatment and Research Clinic at St. Joseph's Healthcare in Hamilton, Ontario.
sentences.zh: 他曾是安大略省汉密尔顿圣约瑟夫医疗中心焦虑治疗与研究中心的创办主任。

sentences.en: Dr. Antony is internationally known for his books and research on anxiety disorders, including phobias,
sentences.zh: 安东尼博士在焦虑症（包括恐惧症）的书籍和研究方面享誉国际，

sentences.en: as well as perfectionism, cognitive behavioral therapy, and assessment of psychological disorders.
sentences.zh: 同时他也精于完美主义、认知行为疗法以及心理障碍评估。

sentences.en: He has published 33 books, including several evidence-based self-help manuals for the general public on overcoming phobias and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 他已出版了 33 本书，其中包括几本面向大众的、关于克服恐惧症和焦虑症的循证自助指南。

sentences.en: Dr. Antony is a fellow of the Royal Society of Canada and a past president of the Canadian Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 安东尼博士是加拿大皇家学会会士，也是加拿大心理学协会前会长。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Antony.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能来，安东尼博士。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me to be here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您邀请我来这里。

sentences.en: Let's start by talking about the difference between a fear and a phobia.
sentences.zh: 让我们先来谈谈恐惧与恐惧症之间的区别。

sentences.en: A phobia is just a more extreme type of fear or are they more complex than that?
sentences.zh: 恐惧症只是更极端的恐惧，还是它们要比这更复杂？

sentences.en: So, a phobia is a fear that, first of all, is excessive.
sentences.zh: 所以，恐惧症首先是一种过度的恐惧。

sentences.en: So, it's out of proportion to the actual danger in the situation.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它与情况本身的实际危险不相称。

sentences.en: But it's also a fear that is causing problems for a person.
sentences.zh: 但这种恐惧同时也在给当事人带来困扰。

sentences.en: So, it's maybe bothering them that they have the fear or it's interfering with their life in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们可能会为自己产生这种恐惧而烦恼，或者它在某种程度上干扰了他们的生活。

sentences.en: So, you may be terrified of snakes, but if you never see a snake, it doesn't really affect what you do in your day-to-day life, then who cares?
sentences.zh: 比如，你可能非常害怕蛇，但如果你从不碰见蛇，它实际上并不影响你的日常生活，那谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: You just have a fear of snakes.
sentences.zh: 你只是怕蛇而已。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if you can't leave your house because you might see a snake
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果你因为可能会看到蛇而不敢出门，

sentences.en: and your fear of snakes is affecting your ability to enjoy a movie or a TV show because there might be a snake on there
sentences.zh: 或者因为里面可能会出现蛇，导致你无法享受电影或电视节目，

sentences.en: or you're having nightmares about snakes that are keeping you awake, then it might be at a level that we might call a phobia.
sentences.zh: 或者你经常做关于蛇的噩梦导致失眠，那么它可能已经达到了我们可以称之为恐惧症的程度。

sentences.en: So, that's one common phobia, snakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是常见的一种恐惧症：怕蛇。

sentences.en: But what are some of the other common phobias and what are the triggers for these phobias?
sentences.zh: 但还有哪些其他的常见恐惧症？这些恐惧症的诱因是什么？

sentences.en: Is there something that ties them together particularly?
sentences.zh: 它们之间有什么特别的共同点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the most common phobia is most likely animal phobias.
sentences.zh: 是的，最常见的恐惧症很可能是动物恐惧症。

sentences.en: So, spiders, snakes, dogs, cats, birds, mice.
sentences.zh: 比如蜘蛛、蛇、狗、猫、鸟、老鼠。

sentences.en: And often among animal phobias, the ones that are most common are the fears of creepy, crawly kinds of things like mice and spiders and snakes and things like that.
sentences.zh: 在动物恐惧症中，最常见的通常是那些令人毛骨悚然、爬来爬去的东西，比如老鼠、蜘蛛、蛇之类的。

sentences.en: Heights would be probably the second most common.
sentences.zh: 恐高症可能是第二常见的。

sentences.en: So, that's very common as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: But we also see lots of people with a fear of flying, a fear of enclosed places, blood, needles, a fear of being in water, fear of storMs.
sentences.zh: 但我们也会看到很多人害怕坐飞机、害怕密闭空间、害怕血液、针头、害怕水、害怕风暴。

sentences.en: So, lots of different things, but those are some of the more common ones.
sentences.zh: 所以涉及各种各样的事情，但这些是比较常见的几种。

sentences.en: And all of these, if you're phobic, it impairs your life, right?
sentences.zh: 所有这些，如果你患有恐惧症，它就会损害你的生活，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just that you're worried that a hurricane is coming because it really is coming,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅仅是你担心飓风要来，因为飓风确实要来了，

sentences.en: but that you spend a lot of time dwelling on this, ruminating over there's going to be a storm.
sentences.zh: 而是你会花大量时间琢磨这事，反反复复地想“要起风暴了”。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, I can't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: “天哪，我哪儿也去不了。”

sentences.en: Yeah, so some of the people I've seen who have come for treatment of storm phobias, it's affecting their life in a few ways.
sentences.zh: 是的，在我接诊的因为风暴恐惧症来求治的患者中，它在几个方面影响了他们的生活。

sentences.en: So, first of all, they're constantly monitoring the weather channel, for example.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们会一直盯着天气频道。

sentences.en: And on days that there are possible storms or even just maybe rain forecast, they may not go to work on those days.
sentences.zh: 在可能有风暴甚至仅仅预报有雨的日子里，他们可能不会去上班。

sentences.en: And then when there is a storm, they may have to hide in their basement so they don't see the lightning through the window.
sentences.zh: 而当风暴来临时，他们可能不得不躲在地下室里，这样就看不到窗外的闪电。

sentences.en: And they have the music blaring so they don't hear the thunder.
sentences.zh: 他们还会把音乐开得震天响，这样就听不到雷声了。

sentences.en: So, it affects their ability to make plans and do the things that they want to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，这影响了他们做计划以及去做自己想做的事情的能力。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so it's affecting their life.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以它确实影响了他们的生活。

sentences.en: And that's what brings people in for help.
sentences.zh: 这也是促使人们寻求帮助的原因。

sentences.en: Where do phobias come from?
sentences.zh: 恐惧症是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Do people just have a bad experience at some point early in life, like, say, a turbulent flight that then leads to fear of flying?
sentences.zh: 人们是否只是在早年经历过某次糟糕的经历，比如经历了一次颠簸的飞行，从而导致了恐飞症？

sentences.en: Or are the origins of phobia less clear-cut than that?
sentences.zh: 还是说恐惧症的起源远没有那么简单明了？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think it really depends on the person.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我觉得这真的因人而异。

sentences.en: So, different people have different pathways to developing fear.
sentences.zh: 不同的人产生恐惧的途径是不同的。

sentences.en: So, three pathways that have been identified.
sentences.zh: 目前已确定有三条途径。

sentences.en: One is a negative experience in the situation.
sentences.zh: 第一种是情境中的负面经历。

sentences.en: So, people have a direct learning experience.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们有了直接的学习体验。

sentences.en: So, maybe they've been bitten by a dog or been in a car accident that leads to a fear of dogs or a fear of driving.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们可能曾被狗咬过，或者经历过车祸，从而导致怕狗或恐车。

sentences.en: But we can also develop phobias through modeling.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以通过榜样作用（观察学习）来产生恐惧症。

sentences.en: And modeling basically just involves watching other people.
sentences.zh: 榜样作用基本上就是指观察其他人。

sentences.en: So, learning through observation.
sentences.zh: 也就是通过观察来学习。

sentences.en: So, if you grow up with parents who are terrified of driving and you see their fear year after year,
sentences.zh: 如果你在父母对开车感到极度恐惧的环境中长大，并且日复一日地看到他们的恐惧，

sentences.en: you know, by the time you get your license, you know, you might be at a higher likelihood of having a fear of driving just from watching them be afraid for so long.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，等你拿到驾照时，仅仅因为长期看着他们感到害怕，你患上恐车症的可能性也许就会更高。

sentences.en: So, we know that children often learn to be afraid by watching other people's responses and situations.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，孩子们经常通过观察其他人在特定情况下的反应来学会害怕。

sentences.en: A third pathway is through information or instruction.
sentences.zh: 第三条途径是通过信息或指示。

sentences.en: And this is learning through language, things that people tell us.
sentences.zh: 这是通过语言以及人们对我们说的话来进行学习。

sentences.en: So, if our parents are always warning us to be careful when we're driving because, you know, you never know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的父母总是警告我们在开车时要小心，因为“你永远不知道会发生什么”。

sentences.en: Or the media certainly can contribute to different fears that people have.
sentences.zh: 或者媒体当然也会助长人们的不同恐惧。

sentences.en: So, that could be another third pathway to developing fear.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是产生恐惧的第三条途径。

sentences.en: So, but I'll just add, those pathways don't affect everybody equally.
sentences.zh: 不过我要补充的是，这些途径并非对每个人都有同样的影响。

sentences.en: So, two people can have a car accident.
sentences.zh: 所以，两个人可能会经历同一场车祸。

sentences.en: One person develops a fear of driving and one doesn't.
sentences.zh: 一个人产生了恐车症，而另一个人没有。

sentences.en: So, we know that there are also other factors, things like genetics, for example, that increase our vulnerability to developing fear following one of these events.
sentences.zh: 因此我们知道，还有其他因素，比如遗传等，它们会增加我们在经历这些事件后产生恐惧的易感性。

sentences.en: And the last thing I want to mention is the role of what we call preparedness.
sentences.zh: 我想提到的最后一点是我们所谓“预备状态”的作用。

sentences.en: And all that means is that through evolution, presumably, we are prepared or predisposed to learn to fear some things more easily than others.
sentences.zh: 这很简单，大概的意思是通过进化，我们做好了准备，或者说有了一种先天倾向，让我们比其他事物更容易学会害怕某些东西。

sentences.en: So, just as an example, almost nobody has a fear of flowers.
sentences.zh: 举个简单的例子，几乎没有人害怕花朵。

sentences.en: But it's very common to have fears of spiders and snakes.
sentences.zh: 但害怕蜘蛛和蛇是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: And the thinking is that spiders and snakes prehistorically would have been more dangerous to our ancestors than flowers would be.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，在史前时期，蜘蛛和蛇对我们祖先的威胁要比花朵更大。

sentences.en: Even modern threats like an electrical socket, you know, theoretically, electrical sockets can be dangerous, but we don't see a lot of people with phobias of electrical sockets.
sentences.zh: 即使是像插座这样的现代威胁，从理论上讲，电插座可能是危险的，但我们并没有看到很多人患有对电插座的恐惧症。

sentences.en: And again, the thinking is that we haven't developed that kind of put that propensity to develop that fear through evolution because they just haven't been around for that long.
sentences.zh: 同样，人们认为我们并没有通过进化发展出产生这种恐惧的倾向，因为它们存在的时间还不够长。

sentences.en: So, our learning plays a role,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的学习经历发挥了一定作用，

sentences.en: but so does our genetics and so does just how we're built in terms of how we've evolved to be more careful around things that are potentially threatening and things that have been threatening for thousands and tens of thousands and hundreds of thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 但我们的基因以及我们的生理构造也同样起作用——也就是我们在进化过程中如何变得更加谨慎，去防范那些潜在的威胁，以及那些已经存在了成千上万年、甚至数十万年的威胁。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about treatment for a minute.
sentences.zh: 那我们花一分钟来谈谈治疗。

sentences.en: What are some of the ways that you can help people overcome phobias?
sentences.zh: 有哪些方法可以帮助人们克服恐惧症？

sentences.en: What is based on scientific evidence that has been shown to work?
sentences.zh: 哪些方法是有科学证据支持并被证明有效的？

sentences.en: So, the most effective treatment is exposure therapy.
sentences.zh: 最有效的治疗方法是暴露疗法。

sentences.en: So, we have all benefited from exposure to overcome a fear of one thing or another.
sentences.zh: 我们都曾受益于暴露来克服这样或那样的恐惧。

sentences.en: You know, one thing I would ask the audience to do is to reflect on, is there anything in their life that they used to be afraid of that they're not afraid of anymore?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想请观众们思考的一个问题是：他们的生活中，是否有什么以前害怕、现在已经不再害怕的东西？

sentences.en: And it might be maybe when they were kids, they were afraid of the dark and now they're not.
sentences.zh: 也许当他们还是孩子的时候，他们害怕黑暗，但现在不害怕了。

sentences.en: Or maybe the first day at work, at their job, they were very nervous meeting new people.
sentences.zh: 或者也许在上班的第一天，在工作中结识新的人时，他们非常紧张。

sentences.en: Or the first time they went on a date with their partner, they were very nervous.
sentences.zh: 或者第一次和伴侣约会时，他们非常紧张。

sentences.en: And it just got easier over time.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，情况变得容易了。

sentences.en: And I might ask them, why did it get easier?
sentences.zh: 我可能会问他们，为什么事情变容易了？

sentences.en: And usually the answer is, well, I just had to do it and it got easier.
sentences.zh: 通常答案是，嗯，我只是硬着头皮去做了，然后就变容易了。

sentences.en: I got used to it.
sentences.zh: 我习惯了。

sentences.en: I learned that the situation wasn't dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我了解到这种情况其实并不危险。

sentences.en: And that's what exposure therapy is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是暴露疗法的全部内容。

sentences.en: We come up with a plan where people gradually expose themselves to the situation or the object that they're afraid of at their own pace.
sentences.zh: 我们制定一个计划，让人们按照自己的节奏，逐渐让自己暴露于他们所害怕的情境或物体中。

sentences.en: We don't force people to do anything.
sentences.zh: 我们不强迫任何人去做任何事。

sentences.en: And again, it's done gradually.
sentences.zh: 而且再次强调，这是一个渐进的过程。

sentences.en: People start at a place where they're willing to.
sentences.zh: 人们从自己愿意接受的起点开始。

sentences.en: And as they become more comfortable, they try things that are more challenging.
sentences.zh: 随着他们感觉越来越舒服，他们会尝试更具挑战性的事情。

sentences.en: So for phobias, that tends to be the main component of treatment.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于恐惧症来说，这往往是治疗的主要组成部分。

sentences.en: There are other strategies that may be useful as well.
sentences.zh: 也可能有其他策略同样有用。

sentences.en: But that would be the most important one for specific phobias in particular.
sentences.zh: 但对于特定恐惧症而言，这将是最重要的一个。

sentences.en: Now, with exposure therapy, is that something you can do on your own or do you need a professional to help you?
sentences.zh: 那么对于暴露疗法，这是你可以独自完成的事情，还是需要专业人士来帮助你？

sentences.en: That is a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So I get asked all the time, if I read your self-help book on how to overcome a phobia, will I overcome it?
sentences.zh: 所以我经常被问到：“如果我读了你写的关于如何克服恐惧症的自助书，我能克服它吗？”

sentences.en: And my answer is it's always the same.
sentences.zh: 我的回答总是千篇一律。

sentences.en: You might say, yes, in the same way that if you read a book on physical fitness, you'll get physically fit.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，是的，就像如果你读了一本关于身体锻炼的书，你就能获得健康的体魄一样。

sentences.en: So in other words, reading the book isn't going to get you over your phobia.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，光是读书并不能帮你克服恐惧症。

sentences.en: You have to do all the things that the book describes.
sentences.zh: 你必须去做书中描述的所有事情。

sentences.en: And some people are able to do that.
sentences.zh: 有些人能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: I get emails from people all over the world who said that the strategies in the book changed their lives.
sentences.zh: 我收到过来自世界各地人们的电子邮件，他们说书中的策略改变了他们的生活。

sentences.en: But we also know from research that many people cannot do it on their own or completely on their own.
sentences.zh: 但我们也从研究中得知，许多人无法靠自己或完全靠自己做到这一点。

sentences.en: They need the support of a therapist who can help to motivate them, help to solve any problems that come up.
sentences.zh: 他们需要治疗师的支持，治疗师可以帮助他们保持动力，并解决出现的任何问题。

sentences.en: In the case of animal phobias, you often need someone else to be controlling the animal and holding the animal.
sentences.zh: 以动物恐惧症为例，你通常需要别人来控制和抓着动物。

sentences.en: Because the client who's afraid of dogs can't go out and find dogs themselves or spiders or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为怕狗的患者自己无法出去找狗、蜘蛛或其他什么东西。

sentences.en: So having somebody there, whether it's a family member or a therapist, to help control the environment and offer support can be useful.
sentences.zh: 因此，有个人在场——无论是家庭成员还是治疗师——来帮助控制环境并提供支持，会很有用。

sentences.en: So I guess the quick answer is some people are able to do it on their own.
sentences.zh: 所以我想简短的回答是：有些人能够靠自己做到。

sentences.en: Other people need the support of a therapist or a family member, somebody to work with them in the situation.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则需要治疗师或家庭成员的支持，需要有人在实际情境中与他们合作。

sentences.en: Are there some phobias that are harder to get over than others?
sentences.zh: 有些恐惧症是不是比其他的更难克服？

sentences.en: Or does it really just depend on the individual who has the phobia?
sentences.zh: 还是说这完全取决于患有恐惧症的个人？

sentences.en: I think it depends a lot on the individual.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上取决于个人。

sentences.en: So I've seen lots of people with the same fear who respond differently to treatment.
sentences.zh: 我见过很多有同样恐惧的人，他们对治疗的反应各不相同。

sentences.en: One thing I would say is that the type of fear does impact on how long it takes to get over it.
sentences.zh: 我要说的一点是，恐惧的类型确实会影响克服它所需的时间。

sentences.en: So there are studies with animal phobias showing that in about two to three hours of exposure, even in a single session, the majority of people can overcome the fear.
sentences.zh: 因此，有针对动物恐惧症的研究表明，大约经过两到三个小时的暴露，甚至在单次治疗中，大多数人就能克服恐惧。

sentences.en: In my experience with driving fears, it takes longer.
sentences.zh: 根据我对驾驶恐惧的经验，这需要更长的时间。

sentences.en: So it might take me about 10 weeks with somebody where they're practicing a lot in between sessions as well to get to that same point.
sentences.zh: 所以对于某个人，我可能需要大约 10 周的时间，期间他们还要在两次治疗之间进行大量练习，才能达到同样的水平。

sentences.en: The other thing I would say is that although most people with a specific phobia can overcome the fear through treatment, more complex kinds of problems like social anxiety,
sentences.zh: 我要说的另一件事是，尽管大多数患有特定恐惧症的人都可以通过治疗克服恐惧，但更复杂的问题，比如社交焦虑症——

sentences.en: where people are nervous in a wide range of social situations, that can take longer to overcome.
sentences.zh: 人们在各种各样的社交场合中都会感到紧张——这可能需要更长的时间才能克服。

sentences.en: And it's not unusual for people to be doing much better at the end of treatment, but still struggling with social anxiety from time to time.
sentences.zh: 治疗结束时情况大有改善，但偶尔仍会与社交焦虑作斗争，这种现象并不罕见。

sentences.en: So it's often a less complete recovery than it would be with something like an animal phobia or a height phobia.
sentences.zh: 因此，与动物恐惧症或恐高症等情况相比，这种恢复往往不那么彻底。

sentences.en: Well, I'm curious about fear of flying as one example, because, I mean, you could go through a lot of the steps that you outline in your books and your manuals.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对恐飞症这个例子很感兴趣，因为，我的意思是，你可以经历你在书和指南中概述的许多步骤。

sentences.en: And, I mean, it just seems really tough if you get to the point where you're on an airplane and you have an attack, a panic attack, essentially, you can't get off the plane.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，如果你到了这样一种地步：身处飞机上并且发作了恐慌——本质上就是恐慌发作，却无法下飞机，那真的会非常艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you work up to getting over fear of flying, which can be very intense for people?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你该如何一步步克服恐飞症？这对人们来说可能非常强烈。

sentences.en: Yeah, so people are afraid of flying for different reasons.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们害怕飞行有不同的原因。

sentences.en: So for some people, it's a fear of the plane crashing.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这是害怕飞机坠毁。

sentences.en: They're not afraid of having a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 他们并不害怕恐慌发作。

sentences.en: They're afraid of the plane itself.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕的是飞机本身。

sentences.en: For other people, they are afraid of having a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 对其他人来说，他们害怕经历恐慌发作。

sentences.en: So I've had, you know, one person said, when I'm on a plane and I'm feeling frightened, I wish the plane would crash.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道的，我曾听一个人说，当他在飞机上感到害怕时，他希望飞机直接坠毁。

sentences.en: You know, for that person, it's not a fear of the plane.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对那个人而言，这并不是对飞机本身的恐惧。

sentences.en: It's a fear of how they feel on the plane.
sentences.zh: 而是对他们在飞机上那种感觉的恐惧。

sentences.en: So, again, having a panic attack and not being able to escape.
sentences.zh: 所以，话说回来，就是经历恐慌发作却无法逃离。

sentences.en: And if that's the case,
sentences.zh: 如果情况是这样的话，

sentences.en: we can often treat people on the ground because people who are afraid of panicking are also afraid of other situations often where they might panic and not be able to get out,
sentences.zh: 我们通常可以在地面上治疗患者，因为害怕恐慌的人，往往也害怕其他可能引发恐慌且无法脱身的处境，

sentences.en: like an enclosed place, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如封闭的空间。

sentences.en: And they're afraid of the panic symptoms themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且他们害怕恐慌的症状本身。

sentences.en: So we can encourage people to experience those symptoms, hyperventilate, you know, breathing really quickly, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以鼓励人们去体验这些症状，比如过度换气，也就是呼吸非常急促，

sentences.en: to get lightheaded or spinning around to get dizzy or running on the spot to get their heart racing.
sentences.zh: 从而感到头晕目眩，或者原地打转来产生眩晕感，或者原地跑步让心跳加速。

sentences.en: And what we find is that as people become less afraid of the symptoms in general,
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，当人们对这些症状的恐惧普遍降低时，

sentences.en: those people also become less afraid of flying because of those when it is due to that fear of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 这些人对飞行的恐惧也会随之减少，因为这种恐惧原本就是由对症状的恐惧引起的。

sentences.en: And there are also strategies we can use with with a fear of panicking.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还可以采取一些针对恐慌恐惧的策略。

sentences.en: That can be other strategies like cognitive strategies where we teach people to identify and challenge some of the thoughts underlying the fear.
sentences.zh: 那可以是其他策略，比如认知策略，我们教导人们识别并挑战那些隐藏在恐惧背后的想法。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people may believe that the sensations are dangerous, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人可能会认为这些身体感觉是危险的，比如说。

sentences.en: So we can help people to reinterpret those sensations as an experience that we all have, but not one that's dangerous necessarily.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以帮助人们重新诠释这些感觉，将其视为我们所有人都会有的体验，而不一定是危险的体验。

sentences.en: So there are other tools we can use as well, in addition to just exposure.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了单纯的暴露疗法外，我们还可以使用其他工具。

sentences.en: Do people who have phobias and use exposure therapy and then feel like they're better, do they have to do some kind of maintenance?
sentences.zh: 那些有恐惧症、接受了暴露疗法并觉得自己康复了的人，他们需要进行某种维持治疗吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do you have to keep practicing in order for the phobia not to recur?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了防止恐惧症复发，你必须持续练习吗？

sentences.en: Um, so fear can return and there are different factors that might contribute to return of fear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，恐惧确实可能会复发，有不同的因素可能会导致恐惧卷土重来。

sentences.en: One is a very long period of not encountering the situation.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是很长一段时间没有遇到那种情境。

sentences.en: Another is having a traumatic experience in the situation.
sentences.zh: 另一个因素是在该情境中遭遇了创伤性经历。

sentences.en: So if you've overcome your fear of driving, then you get into a car accident.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你克服了对开车的恐惧，然后却遭遇了一场车祸。

sentences.en: You might be more likely to have a return of fear.
sentences.zh: 你可能就更有可能再次陷入恐惧。

sentences.en: So we do encourage people to to continue some maintenance exposure to when they have an opportunity to encounter the situation to to do that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实鼓励人们继续进行一些维持性的暴露，每当有机会遇到那种情境时就去这样做。

sentences.en: The other thing I would say is when we are doing therapy, we often encourage people to to continue the exposure, even beyond what they might need to get by in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 我要说的另一件事是，当我们在进行治疗时，通常会鼓励人们继续暴露，甚至超越他们在日常生活中维持现状所需的程度。

sentences.en: So that if a little bit of the fear does return, they can it's manageable.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，即使一小部分恐惧真的复发了，也是可以应付的。

sentences.en: So just as an example, if I'm working with somebody with a fear of spiders, you know,
sentences.zh: 举个简单的例子，如果我正在协助一个有蜘蛛恐惧症的人，你知道的，

sentences.en: we would begin with them standing a few feet away from a spider in a jar and they get closer and closer and eventually hold the jar and then eventually open the jar and spill the spider into a tub and eventually poke the spider.
sentences.zh: 我们会从让他们站在离罐子里的蜘蛛几英尺远的地方开始，然后他们慢慢走近，最终拿着那个罐子，接着把罐子打开，把蜘蛛倒进一个盒子里，最后用东西去碰触那只蜘蛛。

sentences.en: By the end, they're typically holding the spider, even though nobody needs to hold a spider in their everyday life.
sentences.zh: 到最后，他们通常会用手拿着蜘蛛，尽管在日常生活中根本没有人需要去拿蜘蛛。

sentences.en: But if they don't see a spider for a year or two, and a little bit of that fear comes back, there's room for that without it interfering with their life again.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们有一两年没见到蜘蛛，而那一小部分恐惧又回来了，这就有了容纳的空间，而不会再次干扰他们的生活。

sentences.en: And I should mention, we don't use dangerous spiders.
sentences.zh: 我得提一句，我们用的可不是危险的蜘蛛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We're in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我们在加拿大。

sentences.en: We don't have to worry as much about that.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要为那种事操心太多。

sentences.en: But I know that there are people in the audience who have to be careful with the spiders they might encounter in their homes.
sentences.zh: 但我知道听众里有人必须小心他们在家里可能会遇到的蜘蛛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now, I know in recent years, there's been a growing interest in using virtual reality for exposure therapy.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，我知道近年来人们对使用虚拟现实技术来进行暴露疗法的兴趣日益浓厚。

sentences.en: What are the advantages and the disadvantages of VER?
sentences.zh: 虚拟现实技术的优缺点分别是什么？

sentences.en: And is it as effective as real world exposure therapy like you just described?
sentences.zh: 它像你刚才描述的现实世界的暴露疗法一样有效吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the great thing about virtual reality is that you can do it in the therapist's office.
sentences.zh: 所以虚拟现实最大的好处在于你可以在治疗师的办公室里进行。

sentences.en: And before long, people are going to have access to be able to do this in their homes.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，人们将能够在自己家里也能使用这种技术。

sentences.en: In fact, there may already be options where people can just get the software on their own.
sentences.zh: 事实上，可能已经有这样的选项了，人们可以自己获取软件。

sentences.en: And we know that people can buy the head-mounted displays from, you know, Oculus.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们可以从诸如Oculus之类的地方购买头戴式显示器。

sentences.en: And I think Apple is putting something out next year.
sentences.zh: 而且我想苹果公司明年会推出一些新产品。

sentences.en: At least that's what the rumors say.
sentences.zh: 至少传闻是这么说的。

sentences.en: So it will become increasingly accessible and inexpensive over time.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，它会变得越来越容易获取且价格低廉。

sentences.en: The other nice thing about it is that it's just easier.
sentences.zh: 它的另一个好处是更加简便。

sentences.en: If you're afraid of flying, it's not practical to fly three times a week.
sentences.zh: 如果你害怕坐飞机，一周飞三次是不切实际的。

sentences.en: But you could be in a virtual airplane three times a week.
sentences.zh: 但你一周可以身处虚拟飞机中三次。

sentences.en: And there are data to support virtual reality for a range of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 有数据支持虚拟现实技术可用于治疗一系列问题。

sentences.en: I'd say that some of the strongest studies in specific phobias have been in height phobias and flying phobias.
sentences.zh: 我想说，针对特定恐惧症最有力的研究主要集中在恐高症和飞行恐惧症上。

sentences.en: That have found them to be useful.
sentences.zh: 这些研究发现它们是有效的。

sentences.en: There's also data supporting it for public speaking phobias.
sentences.zh: 还有数据支持它用于治疗公众演讲恐惧症。

sentences.en: And the studies that have compared it to live exposure have generally found it to be about equally effective.
sentences.zh: 将它与实景暴露进行对比的研究通常发现两者的疗效大致相当。

sentences.en: And there is a caveat that I want to add is that most of these studies or many of these studies have been done by scientists, researchers, who run virtual reality therapy clinics.
sentences.zh: 不过我想补充一个前提，那就是这些研究中的大部分或许多都是由经营虚拟现实治疗诊所的科学家和研究人员进行的。

sentences.en: So their clients are very invested in virtual reality and they are excited about virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 因此他们的客户对虚拟现实技术投入很深，并且对它充满热情。

sentences.en: So there may be a bit of a bias in that way in terms of who they're studying.
sentences.zh: 所以在研究对象的选择上，这方面可能存在一定的偏差。

sentences.en: I can tell you that in my own experience at our clinic, we found virtual reality to be helpful, but probably not as helpful as the real thing.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，根据我们诊所自身的经验，我们发现虚拟现实确实有帮助，但可能没有真实场景那么有用。

sentences.en: So, again, that's just more anecdotal.
sentences.zh: 所以，话说回来，这更多只是一些个人经验之谈。

sentences.en: But the research generally has supported it.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，研究结果是支持它的。

sentences.en: And I would say we need to see more research and we need to see research in maybe other types of settings as well, where maybe clients are not.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们需要看到更多的研究，并且也需要在其他类型的情境中开展研究，比如患者可能并非如此的情况。

sentences.en: You know, again, if you're going to a VR clinic, you're going to be really excited about doing VR, maybe more so than doing non-VR exposure.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，再次强调，如果你去一家VR诊所，你肯定会对做VR治疗感到非常兴奋，或许比做非VR的暴露治疗更是如此。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Is there a particular age when phobias are likely to develop?
sentences.zh: 恐惧症通常会在哪个特定年龄段发展出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, it really varies across phobias.
sentences.zh: 是的，不同恐惧症的情况真的很不一样。

sentences.en: So things like animal phobias and storm phobias begin very early.
sentences.zh: 像动物恐惧症和风暴恐惧症这些，往往在很小的时候就开始了。

sentences.en: In fact, a lot of people will say, I've had this for as long as I can remember.
sentences.zh: 事实上，很多人会说，我记事起就有这个毛病了。

sentences.en: They have no memory of how it started often.
sentences.zh: 他们通常对它是如何开始的毫无记忆。

sentences.en: At the other extreme would be something like claustrophobia.
sentences.zh: 另一个极端则是像幽闭恐惧症这样的情况。

sentences.en: So it's much more unusual for a young child to be afraid of enclosed places.
sentences.zh: 所以，很小的孩子害怕封闭空间是相当罕见的。

sentences.en: That, on average, tends to begin more in the sort of when someone's in their 20s, on average.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧平均而言往往在人二十多岁的时候开始出现。

sentences.en: It can begin younger, but the average age of onset is much older for claustrophobia.
sentences.zh: 它可能会更早开始，但幽闭恐惧症的发病平均年龄要大得多。

sentences.en: So driving phobia obviously can't begin until you're old enough to drive.
sentences.zh: 所以开车恐惧症显然要在你到了法定开车年龄后才会开始。

sentences.en: So just by definition, just in terms of licensing laws and things.
sentences.zh: 所以这纯粹是由定义决定的，仅仅是从驾照法律之类的角度来看。

sentences.en: So there are some differences, but for sure some phobias begin very, very young.
sentences.zh: 因此确实存在一些差异，但可以肯定的是，有些恐惧症在非常非常小的时候就开始了。

sentences.en: What about sex differences?
sentences.zh: 那性别差异呢？

sentences.en: I was wondering if there might be some phobias that women might have more than men, or maybe
sentences.zh: 我在想，是不是有些恐惧症女性比男性患得更多，或者说

sentences.en: men are socialized to hide their phobias, and so we don't really know what the incidence is.
sentences.zh: 男性在社会化过程中被教导要隐藏恐惧，所以我们实际上并不清楚发病率到底是多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So if we just look at the data on prevalence across men and women, there are differences.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只看男女患病率的数据，确实存在差异。

sentences.en: So some phobias, like animal phobias and storm phobias, again, are much more common in women than men.
sentences.zh: 因此，某些恐惧症，比如动物恐惧症和风暴恐惧症，女性比男性要普遍得多。

sentences.en: Other phobias, like blood and needle phobias, are about equally effective.
sentences.zh: 其他的恐惧症，比如血液和注射恐惧症，男女发病率大致相当。

sentences.en: Some studies have found that we have slightly more effective in women than men, but I would say it's generally much closer compared to something like an animal phobia.
sentences.zh: 有些研究发现女性的患病率比男性略高一点，但我认为与动物恐惧症之类的情况相比，它们总体上要接近得多。

sentences.en: But to your second question, is it possible that men are just under-reporting phobias?
sentences.zh: 但对于你的第二个问题，有没有可能是男性只是隐瞒了他们的恐惧症呢？

sentences.en: And there is an older study that looked at that, that found exactly that.
sentences.zh: 有一项较早的研究探讨过这个问题，并且得出了完全符合这一推测的结果。

sentences.en: What they did is they had people report on phobias, and they found what we typically find, that women were more likely to report having these fears than men.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是让人们报告自己的恐惧症，结果发现了我们通常看到的情况，即女性比男性更有可能报告自己有这些恐惧。

sentences.en: But then they brought them back a few weeks later and did the same questionnaire, but this
sentences.zh: 但随后他们在几周后把这些人叫回来，做了同样的问卷，不过这一次

sentences.en: time they hooked them up to these electrodes and they told them it was a lie detector teSt.
sentences.zh: 他们给这些人接上了电极，并告诉他们这是一次测谎测试。

sentences.en: They told them, we're going to know whether you're telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉受试者：“我们会知道你到底有没有说实话。”

sentences.en: And what they found is that women's fear levels were rated at about the same level, but men reported their fears of snakes and spiders and so on as higher when they thought they
sentences.zh: 结果他们发现，女性的恐惧水平评估结果大致相同，但男性在以为自己会被抓包时，

sentences.en: were going to be caught.
sentences.zh: 报告的对蛇、蜘蛛之类的恐惧程度要高得多。

sentences.en: So anyway, it suggested that men might not be as comfortable reporting their fears unless they know that they're going to be caught.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，这表明男性可能并不那么愿意报告自己的恐惧，除非他们知道自己会被识破。

sentences.en: I should say that, you know, with any kind of research, this is so important, is that we replicate findings.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，对于任何类型的研究来说，有一点极其重要，那就是我们要重复验证研究结果。

sentences.en: There was another study that did not replicate that finding.
sentences.zh: 曾有另一项研究未能重复出那一发现。

sentences.en: So we really, for any kind of research, we can't rely on one study.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于任何类型的研究，我们都不能仅仅依赖单一的研究。

sentences.en: We need to wait until there's three or four or five or six studies that, and look at the pattern across studies.
sentences.zh: 我们需要等待出现三项、四项、五项或六项研究，并观察这些研究之间的一致模式。

sentences.en: So there, there's kind of mixed findings right now.
sentences.zh: 所以目前来看，研究结果可以说是毁誉参半/莫衷一是的。

sentences.en: Um, and if there are, uh, the other question that's relevant though, is what, why are there these gender differences?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果有的话，另一个相关的问题是，为什么会存在这些性别差异呢？

sentences.en: So one possibility is that men are under reporting their fear.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是男性隐瞒了他们的恐惧。

sentences.en: Um, but another possibility is just, uh, our, our social learning.
sentences.zh: 但另一种可能性只是我们的社会学习过程。

sentences.en: So I know when I was growing up, it wasn't unusual to see a woman standing on a chair, screaming if there was a mouse in the room.
sentences.zh: 我记得在我成长过程中，看到一个女人站在椅子上、看到房间里有老鼠就放声尖叫并不是什么罕见的事。

sentences.en: Um, whereas you wouldn't see that with a man, um, and, um, men might also be socialized not to be afraid.
sentences.zh: 然而你在男人身上是不会看到这种情形的，而且，

sentences.en: Maybe they're teased more if they show fear of something.
sentences.zh: 男性的社会化教育也让他们被教导不要害怕。

sentences.en: So they force themselves to do it.
sentences.zh: 也许当他们表现出对某事的恐惧时，受到的嘲笑会更多。

sentences.en: Whereas, uh, in a little girl that might be more acceptable.
sentences.zh: 因此他们强迫自己去克服。

sentences.en: So the thinking is that to the extent that there are gender differences, it has more to do with
sentences.zh: 而在小女孩身上，这种表现可能更容易被接受。

sentences.en: our learning and our socialization than anything to do with, uh, biological differences or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的看法是，如果存在性别差异的话，它更多地与我们的学习和社会化有关，而与生物学差异或诸如此类的东西没有任何关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 对，这说得通。

sentences.en: So we've talked about common phobias, but what are some of the most uncommon phobias?
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论了常见的恐惧症，但有没有一些最不常见的恐惧症呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what is like the strangest phobia you've ever encountered in your work?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在工作中遇到过最奇怪的恐惧症是什么样的？

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So, um, I guess one thing I would say is as common as these common phobias are, it's also common to have uncommon phobias.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我要说的一点是，尽管这些常见的恐惧症很普遍，但拥有不常见的恐惧症也很常见。

sentences.en: So lots, lots of people have phobias that other people don't have.
sentences.zh: 所以有非常多的人患有别人没有的恐惧症。

sentences.en: So it might be, um, a very specific kind of insect, like, uh, I've seen people with a fear of moths.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一种非常特殊的昆虫，比如，我见过有人害怕飞蛾。

sentences.en: Um, I saw, uh, uh, somebody with a fear of buttons, like clothes buttons, um, that if they encountered buttons, they would become very frightened and they would avoid them.
sentences.zh: 我曾见过于某人害怕纽扣，比如衣服上的纽扣，如果他们遇到纽扣就会非常害怕并会刻意避开它们。

sentences.en: And it would just, in every way, it was similar to, uh, uh, a spider phobia or something in that it was very specific to that one situation.
sentences.zh: 在各个方面，这都类似于蜘蛛恐惧症之类的情况，因为它非常具体地针对那一种情境。

sentences.en: It's not like they were generally anxious or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们普遍焦虑或有诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: Um, we once saw somebody who was afraid of the airplanes flying overhead.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经遇到过一个人，他害怕从头顶飞过的飞机。

sentences.en: Um, they could be in an airplane that wasn't frightened to them, but if an airplane was flying
sentences.zh: 他们可以坐在飞机里面而不会感到害怕，但如果有飞机从头顶飞过，

sentences.en: overhead, um, they were frightened and they had to, they were carrying an umbrella and if the umbrella was open, they felt protected.
sentences.zh: 他们就会感到害怕，并且必须随身带着一把伞，如果把伞撑开，他们就会觉得受到保护。

sentences.en: And I don't know if it's because the umbrella blocked their, the vision, like they weren't
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是因为雨伞挡住了他们的视线，让他们

sentences.en: able to see the airplane or if they were afraid something was going to fall out of the plane.
sentences.zh: 看不见飞机，还是因为他们害怕有什么东西会从飞机上掉落下来。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know what, they didn't even know what the fear was.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不知道为什么，他们甚至自己都不知道恐惧究竟是什么。

sentences.en: They just knew that they were afraid.
sentences.zh: 他们只知道自己感到了害怕。

sentences.en: They would panic if an airplane flew overhead.
sentences.zh: 如果有飞机从头顶飞过，他们就会陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: And if they had an umbrella open, they were less afraid.
sentences.zh: 而如果他们撑开一把伞，恐惧感就会减轻。

sentences.en: So those are just a few examples, but again, people can be, uh, and I actually, I did mention, um, that fear of flowers is very uncommon.
sentences.zh: 这些只是几个例子，但话说回来，人们可以……事实上我确实说过，对花的恐惧非常罕见。

sentences.en: Um, we have seen two people with a fear of flowers.
sentences.zh: 我们见过两个害怕花朵的人。

sentences.en: One of them had a fear of sunflowers and, um, she had an experience as a very young child where she was in a sunflower field with her family and she got separated from her family
sentences.zh: 其中一个害怕向日葵，她在很小的时候有过一次经历，当时她和家人在一个向日葵地里，结果跟家人走散了，

sentences.en: and these tall sunflowers were blocking her ability to find her family.
sentences.zh: 那些高大的向日葵挡住了她寻找家人的视线。

sentences.en: And she had a traumatic experience around sunflowers.
sentences.zh: 于是她有了一段围绕向日葵的创伤经历。

sentences.en: The other one was afraid of hollyhocks.
sentences.zh: 另一个人则害怕蜀葵。

sentences.en: Uh, so another very specific kind of flowers.
sentences.zh: 这也是另一种非常特定类型的花。

sentences.en: And she had an experience when she was little where she was chased.
sentences.zh: 她在小时候有过一次经历，当时有人在追她，

sentences.en: Somebody was chasing her and hitting her with hollyhocks.
sentences.zh: 并且用蜀葵打她。

sentences.en: Um, so she developed a very specific fear, also of a very specific flower.
sentences.zh: 所以她产生了一种非常具体的恐惧，同样是对一种非常特定的花朵的恐惧。

sentences.en: And from both of those cases, there was a traumatic experience that caused it.
sentences.zh: 从这两个案例来看，都是某种创伤经历导致了这一结果。

sentences.en: So again, uh, we, we, it's easier to learn to fear spiders or snakes or heights than, than some of these other more unusual things, but it's not impossible to learn to fear these
sentences.zh: 所以话说回来，学会害怕蜘蛛、蛇或高度，要比学会害怕其他这些更不寻常的东西容易得多，但学会害怕这些别的东西并非不可能。

sentences.en: other things.
sentences.zh: 所以说，害怕某种不寻常的事物其实并不罕见。

sentences.en: So it's pretty, it's not unusual to have a fear of something that's unusual.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我在这里笑了一下，但我理解这其实是件严肃的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'm laughing a little bit here, but I understand that, that this is serious stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人的生活正是因为这些恐惧而受到了严重影响。

sentences.en: I mean, these are people whose lives have been, um, impinged upon because of the fears.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人的生活正是因为这些恐惧而受到了严重影响。

sentences.en: And, and I don't want to, uh, discount that.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且我并不想，呃，贬低这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, this really is, we're not, you know, just being silly here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是，我们不是，你知道的，只是在这里瞎胡闹。

sentences.en: I'm not just being silly here.
sentences.zh: 我不是在这里瞎胡闹。

sentences.en: I should say, let me ask you, um, is there a relationship between specific phobias and other anxiety disorders like social phobia or agoraphobia, which for our listeners is
sentences.zh: 我应该说，请问您，呃，特定恐惧症与其他焦虑症（比如社交恐惧症或广场恐惧症，对我们的听众来说，广场恐惧症就是

sentences.en: just the fear of being in public or crowded spaces?
sentences.zh: 害怕身处公共场所以及拥挤的空间）之间是否存在某种关联？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we, we looked at this, uh, years ago, I think when I was still a graduate student in the 1990s, I think we published a paper on this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，我们研究过这个，呃，很多年前，我想大概是我在上世纪90年代读研究生的时候，我们好像就此发表过一篇论文。

sentences.en: And what we found was that, uh, they often go hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 我们的发现是，呃，它们经常是相伴而生的。

sentences.en: It's not unusual for people to have a specific phobia as well as some other problem.
sentences.zh: 人们既有特定恐惧症，同时又存在其他问题，这并不少见。

sentences.en: But if the most severe problem that they have is a specific phobia, that tends to be the only thing they have.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们最严重的问题是特定恐惧症，那么这往往也是他们唯一的心理问题。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if the most severe anxiety problem they have is something else like social
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果他们最严重的焦虑问题是其他方面的，比如社交

sentences.en: anxiety or panic disorder, OCD or something, the specific phobia, um, they'll often have an additional specific phobia of lesser severity.
sentences.zh: 焦虑、恐慌症、强迫症或类似问题，那么至于特定恐惧症，呃，他们往往还会伴有某种严重程度较低的特定恐惧症。

sentences.en: And the way we interpret that is basically to say that when, uh, specific phobias are, are, they tend to be less severe than some of the other anxiety probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们的理解基本上是说，当，呃，特定恐惧症，它们的严重程度往往低于其他一些焦虑问题。

sentences.en: So when people do have both, it's the other problem.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们两者兼有时，往往是另一个问题。

sentences.en: That's usually the one that's interfering the most with their life.
sentences.zh: 那个问题通常对他们的生活影响最大。

sentences.en: Um, and that's why specific phobias, even though they're, they're the most common or among the most common anxiety problem that people can have, they're the least likely to
sentences.zh: 呃，这就是为什么特定恐惧症，尽管它们是，它们是最常见的或者说人们可能患有的最常见的焦虑问题之一，它们却最不大会

sentences.en: show up for treatment.
sentences.zh: 去寻求治疗。

sentences.en: Um, for most people, even though it interferes somewhat with their life from time to time, they can get by.
sentences.zh: 呃，对大多数人来说，尽管它偶尔会对生活造成一些干扰，但他们还是能应付过去的。

sentences.en: Um, whereas something like social anxiety might affect everything, their ability to form relationships, their ability to work and, and, and things like that, a fear of spiders
sentences.zh: 呃，相比之下，像社交焦虑可能会影响方方面面，比如他们建立人际关系的能力、工作能力，等等诸如此类，而对蜘蛛的恐惧

sentences.en: might affect places you can go.
sentences.zh: 可能会影响你能去的地方。

sentences.en: It might, uh, keep you up at night sometimes, but it's not, it had, the, the impact is more manageable, uh, than it would be for some of these other problems on average.
sentences.zh: 它可能会，呃，让你有时夜不能寐，但它的影响没有那么大，平均而言，其影响比其他一些问题要更容易控制，呃。

sentences.en: Again, there's always exceptions.
sentences.zh: 当然，总是有例外的。

sentences.en: I saw, I've seen people with medical phobias, for example, who can't get life saving surgery because their fear of needles or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我见过，比方说，我见过患有医疗恐惧症的人，他们因为害怕针头之类的东西而无法接受救命的手术。

sentences.en: So, um, but for the average, the average person with a specific phobia, they, they're more
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，但对于一般人来说，对于患有特定恐惧症的普通人，他们更

sentences.en: likely to make either not seek treatment because they're not sure where to get it, or, or even if they know where they can get it, they, they'd rather just live with the fear.
sentences.zh: 倾向于不去寻求治疗，要么是因为他们不确定去哪里治疗，要么是即使他们知道去哪里治疗，他们也宁愿带着恐惧继续生活。

sentences.en: So what are the next big research questions for you?
sentences.zh: 那么，对您来说接下来的重大研究课题是什么？

sentences.en: What are you looking at now?
sentences.zh: 您目前在关注什么？

sentences.en: So, um, a lot of, uh, my work is, is very broad.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我的很多，呃，工作都非常广泛。

sentences.en: So, um, I, I, I'm not currently doing any work in specific phobias, uh, in particular, currently we're doing some research in perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我，我目前并没有在特定恐惧症领域做任何工作，呃，特别地，目前我们正在做一些关于完美主义的研究。

sentences.en: We're doing some research on social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们在做一些关于社交焦虑的研究。

sentences.en: Uh, one of the studies that one of my graduate students is working on right now is looking at the relationship between experiences of racism and discrimination in black women and
sentences.zh: 呃，我的一个研究生目前正在进行的一项研究是，探讨黑人女性遭遇种族主义和歧视的经历及其对

sentences.en: their impact on social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 社交焦虑的影响。

sentences.en: Uh, so that's one, one project going on in the lab.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是实验室正在进行的其中一个项目。

sentences.en: Um, and then we have a couple of projects going on in perfectionism, looking at perfectionism
sentences.zh: 呃，然后我们还有几个关于完美主义的项目，比如研究完美主义

sentences.en: and problem, problem gaming, for example, looking at the impact of perfectionism in, uh, friendships.
sentences.zh: 与问题游戏行为的关系，研究完美主义在，呃，友谊中的影响。

sentences.en: Um, so we are actually, we are developing a new measure of specific phobias to measure severity.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以实际上，我们正在开发一种测量特定恐惧症严重程度的新量表。

sentences.en: So this will be a tool that would be helpful for researchers to look at changes in specific phobia levels as a result of treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一个有用的工具，帮助研究人员观察治疗后特定恐惧症水平的变化。

sentences.en: Um, so that's, that's ongoing right now.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以这个项目目前正在进行中。

sentences.en: Uh, we've been doing some research on anxiety and COVID.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们一直在做一些关于焦虑与新冠疫情的研究。

sentences.en: Um, so we did, I said, I'm not doing work in specific phobias, but I am.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以刚才我说我没有在做特定恐惧症的研究，但其实我在做。

sentences.en: Um, we just, um, uh, finished a study.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们刚刚，呃，完成了一项研究。

sentences.en: It's under review right now.
sentences.zh: 目前正在接受同行评审。

sentences.en: Um, looking at claustrophobia and mask wearing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 呃，探讨新冠肺炎大流行期间的幽闭恐惧症与佩戴口罩的关系。

sentences.en: Um, so that, that is a project related to specific phobias for sure.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以这，这绝对是一个与特定恐惧症相关的项目。

sentences.en: Um, and then a lot of my time right now is spent, uh, um, leading a provincial program here in
sentences.zh: 呃，我现在的很多时间都花在，呃，领导安大略省的

sentences.en: Ontario aimed at getting evidence-based treatments for anxiety problems to people across the
sentences.zh: 一个全省项目上，旨在向全省民众提供针对焦虑问题的循证治疗，

sentences.en: province in a, uh, a stepped care model where people begin with a more self-directed approach and then step up to a therapist-directed approach, um, if needed.
sentences.zh: 采用的是阶梯式照护模式，即人们从更具自我导向的方法开始，如果需要的话，再进阶到由治疗师指导的方法。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, the, the big challenge in, in anxiety, you know, we now have effective treatments and we're always tweaking them to see if we can get them a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 呃，而且你知道，焦虑症领域最大的挑战，你知道，我们现在有了有效的治疗方法，我们也在不断调整它们，看看能不能让疗效更好一点。

sentences.en: Um, but the biggest challenge is getting them to the people who need them.
sentences.zh: 呃，但最大的挑战是把它们送到需要它们的人手中。

sentences.en: And, um, that's what this, this other big project is, uh, provincial project involves seeing if we can, uh, get the help to people who need it, uh, the moSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，这就是这个，这个其他重大项目，也就是全省项目所要做的事情，看看我们是否能，呃，把帮助送到最需要的人手中。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you for joining me today, Dr. Anthony.
sentences.zh: 好的，安东尼博士，我要感谢您今天能来。

sentences.en: I think this is very interesting and I appreciate that there are effective treatments and I think
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有趣，我也很高兴现在有有效的治疗方法，并且我觉得

sentences.en: we can put some information in the notes that go along with the podcast, uh, directing people
sentences.zh: 我们可以在播客的备注里附上一些信息，呃，指引人们

sentences.en: to some of the publications that you have out there that will tell people how to take care of themselves if they've got a phobia.
sentences.zh: 阅读您发表的一些出版物，这些出版物会告诉人们如果患有恐惧症该如何进行自我护理。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed being here and, um, all the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里，呃，祝一切顺利。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
